parts.note: E is the standard abbreviation for English
U is the usual abbreviation for university
nice is a plain synonym of pleasant

explanation.surface: A woman discovers that an English university is an agreeable place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' looks like the subject of the sentence but is the definition: any woman's name will do, here EUNICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Eunice is a female first name, so a pronoun for a woman can stand for it in crossword convention.

clue.text: Old address of Turkish civil service

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a former courtesy title, like 'sir', in the Ottoman Empire

definitions.note: the service defines one of its members, an official
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a title for an educated official of the Ottoman state

explanation.walkthrough: 'Address' is a form of address, a title, not a street location; it was used for officials of the Ottoman government.
explanation.definitionFit: The word was a Turkish honorific for men of standing, especially government officials and scholars.

clue.text: No, I am wrong, she was Ruth's mother-in-law

indicators.note: something wrong is out of its proper state, so these letters are set in a different order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A woman denying an identity, corrected by a note on who she was in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Old Testament Book of Ruth, the Moabite Ruth stays loyal to her husband's mother after he dies.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: established practices or traditions
second meaning: taxes levied on imported goods

explanation.walkthrough: 'Duties' looks like daily chores paired with habits, but it means import taxes.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural word means both usual practices of a society and charges paid at the border on imports.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the human spirit or mind
second meaning: the mortal princess loved by Cupid in Greek myth

explanation.walkthrough: 'Soul mate' reads as one phrase about a romantic partner, but the split falls between the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek word for the human spirit is also the name of the girl whom the love god married in myth.

clue.text: Burning waste on a huge scale

definitions.text: Burning waste on a huge scale

parts.words: Burning waste on a huge scale
parts.note: surface reading: rubbish incinerated in vast quantities

parts.words: Burning waste on a huge scale
parts.note: setter's reading: an enormous scorching wasteland, that is a vast hot desert

explanation.walkthrough: 'Burning' looks like a verb and 'waste' like rubbish; read instead as a burning-hot waste, a barren expanse.
explanation.definitionFit: The great North African desert is the largest hot desert on Earth, an immense scorching barren land.

indicators.note: without is used in its old sense of outside, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: to cite someone is to call them, for instance to court
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone summoned without warning turns snobbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' reads as 'lacking', but here it means 'outside': the word for called wraps round once.
explanation.definitionFit: Conceited means vain or excessively proud of oneself, much like a stuck-up person.

clue.text: Noise or disturbance can be wearing

indicators.note: a disturbance throws things into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Constant noise or interruption can be tiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wearing' looks like the adjective meaning tiring; it is the noun for wearing away.
explanation.definitionFit: Erosion is the gradual wearing away of rock or soil by wind, water or ice.

clue.text: It was frightful, as a rule

definitions.text: It was frightful, as a rule

parts.words: It was frightful, as a rule
parts.note: surface reading: something that was usually dreadful

parts.words: It was frightful, as a rule
parts.note: setter's reading: a period of government that ruled through fear

explanation.walkthrough: 'As a rule' seems to mean 'usually'; read literally it means 'as a period of rule', the bloody phase of the French Revolution in 1793 to 1794.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name for the Jacobin government's period of mass executions during the French Revolution, rule by fear.

parts.note: surface reading: a hairdresser deciding what form to cut
setter's reading: the name of a rounded, bushy style of curly hair

explanation.walkthrough: Any number of hairstyles fit; the short length and the idea of a distinctive round shape point to the one meant.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a style in which naturally tightly curled hair is grown out into a rounded halo shape.

parts.note: surface reading: an engineer who builds space rockets
setter's reading: the man behind Rocket, the famous early steam locomotive of 1829

explanation.walkthrough: Rocket was the locomotive built by George and Robert Stephenson that won the 1829 Rainhill Trials in England; the capital R is the giveaway.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stephensons, father and son, built the steam engine named Rocket, so they were literally its designers.

clue.text: No rice pudding for Caruso, for instance

indicators.note: a pudding is a mixture stirred together, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A famous tenor is refused his dessert of rice pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: Caruso was the great Italian tenor whose first name was ENRICO; 'for instance' marks him as one example of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Enrico Caruso is a famous bearer of the Italian forename, so he is an instance of it.

clue.text: Growing area, one with a shrub

parts.note: a plot where plants are grown
Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A description of a planted area containing a single bush.
explanation.definitionFit: The gardenia is an evergreen flowering bush grown for its fragrant white blooms.

clue.text: In a difficult situation, use hose on grass

parts.note: hose is an old word for stockings or tights
grass and pot are both slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: An instruction to water a lawn with a garden hose when stuck in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hose' and 'grass' suggest gardening, but they are legwear and cannabis. To be 'in a difficult situation' is to be in a tight spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A tight spot is an idiom for an awkward predicament from which escape is hard.

parts.note: surface reading: a dubious or suspect welcome
setter's reading: a salutation that takes the form of a question

explanation.walkthrough: 'Questionable' usually means doubtful; here it means phrased as a question.
explanation.definitionFit: This everyday salutation asks after someone's health, so it is a greeting that is literally a question.

indicators.note: to turn something round is to make it face the other way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: nut is slang for the head

explanation.surface: People's heads swivel round in surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun someone is to daze or stupefy them, as a sudden shock does.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the hood worn by a monk
second meaning: a hooded cover on a chimney that stops it blowing smoke back down

explanation.walkthrough: Monkshood is also a poisonous plant, which makes 'a cure for smoking' sound medicinal; but it is read as a monk's hood, and the smoking is a chimney's.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a monastic hooded garment and a revolving metal hood fitted over a chimney pot to improve its draught.

definitions.note: an adjective defining a noun: the animal is known for being sure-footed
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a nimble goat-antelope of European mountains
second meaning: soft leather used for polishing glass

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a steady person on a ladder; instead it is a mountain animal and the leather made from its skin.
explanation.definitionFit: The agile Alpine goat-antelope gives its name to the soft leather cloth used to polish panes.

definitions.note: a verb phrase defining an adjective: someone stone-deaf can't hear

indicators.note: letters that fade away drift off and fall out of their order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone straining to catch music as the notes die out.
explanation.definitionFit: Stone-deaf means completely without hearing, the state of a person who cannot hear at all.

indicators.note: putting things in order means arranging them, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.definitionFit: Nemesis, from the Greek goddess of vengeance, means deserved punishment that cannot be escaped.

parts.note: surface reading: a lover betrays a figure from Scripture
setter's reading: the famous medieval lover's name gives away, that is reveals, a Bible figure at its start

explanation.walkthrough: Peter Abelard was the 12th-century French scholar famed for his love affair with Heloise; his name starts with ABEL, son of Adam, so it gives that character away. The rest of the name has no clue words.
explanation.definitionFit: Abelard is remembered as one of history's great tragic romantics through his letters with Heloise.

clue.text: Macbeth, for example, goes after final piece of fuel

indicators.note: final means the last, so only the closing letter of the word is used

parts.note: the closing letter of piece
Macbeth was Thane of Glamis and of Cawdor, a Scottish noble title

explanation.surface: Macbeth hunting down the last scrap of fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes after' means placed after: the noble comes after the letter. 'Final piece of fuel' wants to be the last letter of fuel, but 'of fuel' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethane is a flammable hydrocarbon gas found in natural gas and burned for energy.

clue.text: He has a telling part in play

definitions.text: He has a telling part in play

parts.words: He has a telling part in play
parts.note: surface reading: an actor whose role is especially significant

parts.words: He has a telling part in play
parts.note: setter's reading: a role whose job is literally to tell the story

explanation.walkthrough: 'Telling' usually means striking or revealing; here it means recounting, which is what this character does on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the performer who relates the story to the audience, so his part consists of telling.

clue.text: No one scores with this girl

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in cricket, an over in which no runs are scored
second meaning: an old word for a young unmarried woman

explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at an unattainable girl. In cricket, a maiden over is a set of six balls from which the batsmen score no runs.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a cricketing term for a scoreless over and an old-fashioned noun for a young woman.

clue.text: Initially it may be uphill, even steep

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so each word contributes its opening letter

parts.note: opening letters of these five words

explanation.surface: A warning that a path may climb at first and even be steep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steep' looks like the adjective describing the hill; it is the verb meaning to soak.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbue is to saturate or soak something thoroughly, as when cloth is steeped in dye.

parts.note: surface reading: excessively friendly or familiar
setter's reading: having more than one mate, that is more than one spouse

explanation.walkthrough: 'Matey' normally means chummy; read as 'taking mates', too much of it means having several wives or husbands at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Polygamous describes someone married to several partners simultaneously, taking too many spouses.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ray or shaft of light
second meaning: a thick length of wood supporting a building

explanation.walkthrough: 'Light or heavy' looks like a choice of weights for the timber; the light is illumination, not lightness.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a narrow shaft of radiance and a large structural joist of wood.

parts.note: surface reading: a servant who pours and hands round wine
setter's reading: the small dish that a teacup literally sits on

explanation.walkthrough: A cup-bearer is a royal servant, but the question mark invites a literal reading of something that bears a cup.
explanation.definitionFit: This shallow dish holds up a teacup, so it is quite literally the thing that carries a cup.

indicators.note: wild things are unruly and out of control, so the letters run riot

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Rising to one's feet to join in some frenzied dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascend is to rise or climb upward, a formal equivalent of standing or going up.
